rules.runtime_check: Compare the hidden select's <option> list and value against the custom UI's options and displayed value; change the selection and assert they stay equal.

rules.rule: The hidden `<select>` includes form attributes as needed (e.g., `name`, `required`, `disabled`).
rules.static_hint: Hidden select carries name (and required/disabled when the field's contract calls for them).
rules.llm_eval_question: Given the field's form behavior, are the appropriate form attributes present on the hidden select?

rules.rule: The hidden `<select>` is not focusable (so users don't tab to both controls).
rules.static_hint: Hidden select carries tabindex="-1" (or an equivalent focus exclusion).
rules.runtime_check: Tab through the field; assert only the custom button receives focus, never the hidden select.

rules.rule: The visible interactive control is a native `<button>` (preferred) or `role="button"` only when a native button cannot be used.
rules.static_hint: Visible trigger is a native <button>, or role="button" as documented fallback.
rules.llm_eval_question: If role="button" is used, is there a genuine constraint that prevented a native <button>?

rules.rule: If using `role="button"`, add `tabindex="0"`
rules.static_hint: role="button" trigger also carries tabindex="0".

rules.rule: If using `role="button"`, add keyboard support for Enter and Space.
rules.static_hint: role="button" trigger has key handlers covering Enter and Space.
rules.runtime_check: Focus the role="button" trigger, press Enter, then Space; assert each opens the listbox.

rules.rule: ensuring Space prevents page scrolling while activating.
rules.runtime_check: On a scrollable page, press Space on the focused role="button" trigger; assert activation occurs and the page does not scroll.

rules.rule: The button must expose "opens a listbox" semantics and state: `aria-haspopup="listbox"`
rules.static_hint: Button carries aria-haspopup with the exact value "listbox".

rules.rule: `aria-expanded="true|false"` reflecting open/closed
rules.static_hint: Button carries aria-expanded bound to popup state.
rules.runtime_check: Open and close the listbox; assert aria-expanded always matches actual visibility.

rules.rule: `aria-controls="IDREF"` pointing to the listbox element
rules.static_hint: Button's aria-controls IDREF resolves to the role="listbox" element.

rules.rule: The button must have an accessible name that includes the field label and current value.
rules.static_hint: Button's name computation draws on both the label element and a current-value element.
rules.runtime_check: Compute the button's accessible name; assert it contains the field label followed by the currently selected value, and updates when the value changes.

rules.rule: Recommended: `aria-labelledby="{labelId} {valueId}"` where `labelId` references the label element and `valueId` references an element containing the currently selected value text
rules.static_hint: Button's aria-labelledby lists the label element's id first, then the value element's id, both resolving.

rules.rule: The popup contains one element with `role="listbox"` and a stable ID (the same one referenced by `aria-controls`).
rules.static_hint: Exactly one role="listbox" element with an id matching the button's aria-controls.

rules.rule: Each option uses `role="option"` and has a stable ID.
rules.static_hint: Every option carries role="option" and a deterministic id usable by aria-activedescendant.

rules.rule: Each option exposes selection with `aria-selected="true|false"`.
rules.static_hint: Every option carries aria-selected bound to selection state.
rules.runtime_check: Change the selection; assert aria-selected="true" moves to the newly selected option only.

rules.rule: When the listbox is open, the "currently active" option is programmatically indicated (recommended). Preferred approach: keep focus on the button and set `aria-activedescendant="{optionId}"` on the button to point to the active option.
rules.static_hint: Button carries aria-activedescendant bound to the active option's id while open.
rules.runtime_check: Open the listbox and arrow through options; assert DOM focus stays on the button and aria-activedescendant always resolves to the highlighted option.

rules.rule: The listbox must be shown/hidden in the DOM so that when closed it cannot be reached by keyboard or screen readers (e.g., via `hidden`).
rules.static_hint: Closed state uses `hidden`/conditional rendering/display:none.
rules.runtime_check: With the listbox closed, assert its options are unreachable and absent from the accessibility tree.

rules.rule: Tab / Shift+Tab moves focus to/from the button like a normal form field (no focus trap).
rules.runtime_check: Tab into and out of the field in both directions; assert focus moves like a native form field with no trapping.

rules.rule: Enter or Space on the button opens the listbox.
rules.runtime_check: Press Enter (and separately Space) on the focused button; assert the listbox opens.

rules.rule: When open: Arrow Up/Down moves the active option.
rules.runtime_check: With the listbox open, press Arrow Down/Up; assert the active option advances/retreats one option per press.

rules.rule: When open: Enter or Space selects the active option and closes the listbox.
rules.runtime_check: Press Enter (and separately Space) on an active option; assert it becomes selected, the listbox closes, and the button's value text updates.

rules.rule: When open: Esc closes the listbox and returns the user to the button state.
rules.runtime_check: With the listbox open, press Esc; assert it closes without changing the selection and focus remains on the button.

rules.rule: Clicking/tapping outside closes the listbox.
rules.runtime_check: With the listbox open, click outside the component; assert the listbox closes.

rules.rule: The label and current value are announced together (via `aria-labelledby`).
rules.static_hint: aria-labelledby composes label + value elements.
rules.runtime_check: Compute the button's accessible name; assert it contains both the label and the current value.

rules.rule: Expanded/collapsed state is announced (via `aria-expanded`).
rules.static_hint: aria-expanded present on the button.
rules.runtime_check: Assert the button's expanded state in the accessibility tree tracks the popup's open/closed state.

rules.rule: The user can perceive which option is selected (`aria-selected`).
rules.static_hint: aria-selected present on options.
rules.runtime_check: Assert the selected option's aria-selected="true" matches the visible selection.

rules.rule: The user can perceive which option is currently active when navigating (`aria-activedescendant` recommended).
rules.static_hint: aria-activedescendant (or equivalent focus indication) present while navigating.
rules.runtime_check: Arrow through options; assert the active option is programmatically exposed at each step.

rules.rule: Do not omit the visually hidden native `<select>` when this control participates in form submission or should support autofill.
rules.static_hint: If the component sits in a <form> or has a name-able value, a hidden native <select> must be present.
rules.llm_eval_question: Does this select participate in form submission or autofill, and if so, is the hidden native select present?

rules.rule: Do not implement the trigger as a non-interactive element (e.g., `<div>`) without button semantics.
rules.static_hint: Flag click handlers on trigger elements lacking <button> or role="button"+tabindex.

rules.rule: Do not use `role="menu"` / `role="menuitem"` for select options.
rules.static_hint: Flag menu/menuitem roles in the popup; require listbox/option.

rules.rule: Do not make each option tabbable (avoid forcing users to Tab through options).
rules.static_hint: Flag tabindex="0" on option elements.
rules.runtime_check: With the listbox open, press Tab; assert focus leaves the component rather than stepping through options.

rules.rule: Do not leave the listbox visible while `aria-expanded="false"` (and vice versa).
rules.runtime_check: Across open/close cycles, assert listbox visibility and the button's aria-expanded never disagree.

rules.rule: Do not allow the custom UI and hidden `<select>` to get out of sync (options/value must match).
rules.runtime_check: After every selection change (keyboard and pointer), assert the hidden select's value and options equal the custom UI's.

rules.rule: Use a native `<select>` element with native `<option>` elements.
rules.static_hint: Control is a native <select> whose children are <option> (or <optgroup>) elements.

rules.rule: Provide a visible label associated with the `<select>` via a native `<label>` using `for`/`id`.
rules.static_hint: A <label for> / htmlFor points at the select's id, or the select is wrapped in a <label>.
rules.runtime_check: Assert the label renders visible and resolves into the select's computed accessible name.

rules.rule: The `<select>` participates in the form via a `name` attribute, and uses native attributes (`required`, `disabled`) as needed.
rules.static_hint: The select carries a name attribute; required and disabled use the native attributes rather than aria-required or aria-disabled.

rules.rule: Keep option content as plain text.
rules.static_hint: <option> elements contain text only — no elements, images, or markup.

rules.rule: Style the control with CSS only (`appearance` and related properties).
rules.static_hint: Styling is applied through CSS on the native select; no scripted re-implementation of the control's appearance or behavior.

rules.rule: Do not use the `multiple` attribute (native multi-select tests very poorly).
rules.static_hint: Flag the multiple attribute on the select.

rules.rule: The switch has `role="switch"`.
rules.static_hint: Control carries role="switch" (or is an input[type="checkbox"] with role="switch").

rules.rule: The switch has a visible text label, either programmatically associated with the control (`label[for]`) or matched by an accessible name on the control (`aria-label` or `aria-labelledby`).
rules.static_hint: A labelling mechanism is authored: label[for], aria-labelledby, aria-label, or a wrapping label.
rules.runtime_check: Render the switch; assert the label text is visible and its computed accessible name is non-empty and derived from that label.

rules.rule: The accessible name begins with the visible label text, and may append a short amount of additional context for screen reader users (via `aria-label`, `aria-labelledby`, or offscreen `.sr-only` text).
rules.runtime_check: Compute the switch's accessible name and assert it begins with the visible label text.

rules.rule: The accessible name describes the setting the switch controls, worded so it is true when the switch is on (e.g., "Enable notifications").
rules.llm_eval_question: Does the accessible name name the setting being controlled, phrased so it reads true when the switch is on, rather than being vague or stateful ("On", "Toggle")?

rules.rule: The switch's on/off state is exposed via `aria-checked` (`"true"`/`"false"`), or via the native `checked` property when the switch is an `input[type="checkbox"]`.
rules.static_hint: Exactly one state mechanism is authored: aria-checked bound to state, or the native checked property on an input[type="checkbox"].

rules.rule: The exposed state stays in sync with the switch as it toggles.
rules.runtime_check: Toggle the switch repeatedly; assert aria-checked (or native checked) matches the rendered on/off state after every toggle.

rules.rule: The switch is focusable so Tab and Shift+Tab reach it: a native `input[type="checkbox"]` is focusable by default; a non-native element (`div`/`button` with `role="switch"`) must include `tabIndex="0"`.
rules.static_hint: Switch is a natively focusable element, or a non-native element carrying tabindex="0".
rules.runtime_check: Tab and Shift+Tab through the page; assert the switch receives focus from both directions (catches an inert or hidden ancestor that markup alone cannot reveal).

rules.rule: Space toggles the switch.
rules.runtime_check: Focus the switch and press Space; assert the state toggles and the page does not scroll.

rules.rule: Enter toggles the switch.
rules.runtime_check: Focus the switch and press Enter; assert the state toggles. Exception: for a native input[type="checkbox"] implementation, Enter is not expected to toggle — assert Space alone does.

rules.rule: If multiple switches are presented as a labeled set, group them with `fieldset` + `legend` or `role="group"` + `aria-labelledby`.
rules.static_hint: A set of sibling switches is wrapped in fieldset+legend or role="group"+aria-labelledby.
rules.llm_eval_question: Do these switches form a labeled set that a user would read as one group, and if so, is the group structure present?

rules.rule: The group's label describes the purpose of the set (WCAG 2.4.6).
rules.llm_eval_question: Does the legend or group label describe what the set of switches is for, rather than being generic or a restatement of one member?

rules.rule: Associate any additional descriptive static text with the switch via `aria-describedby` on the switch element itself.
rules.static_hint: Descriptive text is referenced by aria-describedby on the switch element, with a matching id authored.
rules.runtime_check: Assert the aria-describedby IDREF resolves to a rendered element and contributes the expected description.

rules.rule: Do not place `aria-describedby` on a `fieldset` or group container.
rules.static_hint: Flag aria-describedby authored on a fieldset or [role="group"] container rather than on the switch.

rules.rule: Do not use a switch for non-setting actions; use it only for persistent on/off settings.
rules.llm_eval_question: Does this control persist an on/off setting, or does it fire a one-shot action or navigation (which should be a button)?

rules.rule: Do not use both `checked` and `aria-checked` on `input[type="checkbox"]`.
rules.static_hint: Flag a checkbox input that carries both the native checked property and aria-checked.

rules.rule: The set of tabs is contained in an element with `role="tablist"`.
rules.static_hint: A container element carries role="tablist".

rules.rule: Each tab has `role="tab"` and is contained within the tablist.
rules.static_hint: Every element with role="tab" is a descendant of the role="tablist" container.

rules.rule: Each tab uses a native `<button>` as its base element (preferred), or a non-native element with `role="tab"` only when a native button cannot be used.
rules.static_hint: Each role="tab" element is a <button>, or a non-native element carrying role="tab".

rules.rule: If a non-native element is used, add `tabindex` and keyboard support for Enter and Space, ensuring Space prevents page scrolling while activating the tab.
rules.static_hint: Non-native tab elements carry a tabindex attribute and a keydown handler covering Enter and Space with preventDefault on Space.
rules.runtime_check: Focus a non-native tab and press Space; assert the tab activates and the page scroll position is unchanged.

rules.rule: Each panel is an element with `role="tabpanel"`.
rules.static_hint: One element with role="tabpanel" exists per tab.

rules.rule: Exactly one tabpanel is displayed at a time.
rules.runtime_check: Activate each tab in turn; after each activation assert exactly one role="tabpanel" element is visible.

rules.rule: Each tabpanel is shown/hidden in the DOM (e.g., via the `hidden` attribute), so that when hidden, its content cannot be reached by keyboard or screen readers.
rules.static_hint: Inactive tabpanels carry the hidden attribute, display: none, or are not rendered; they are not merely positioned offscreen.
rules.runtime_check: With one tab selected, assert every other tabpanel is absent from the accessibility tree and that no element inside it can receive focus via Tab.

rules.rule: A vertically stacked tablist has `aria-orientation="vertical"`; a horizontal tablist omits the attribute.
rules.static_hint: aria-orientation="vertical" is present when the tablist is laid out vertically and absent when it is laid out horizontally.
rules.llm_eval_question: When the layout cannot be resolved from the markup alone, do the applied styles render the tablist vertically, and does the attribute match?

rules.rule: The tablist has an accessible name, via `aria-labelledby` referencing a visible heading when one exists, otherwise via `aria-label`.
rules.static_hint: The role="tablist" element carries aria-labelledby or aria-label; any aria-labelledby target id exists in the document.
rules.runtime_check: Compute the tablist's accessible name; assert it is non-empty.

rules.rule: Each tab's visible text is contained in its accessible name, and appears at the start of it when additional context is appended.
rules.static_hint: Any aria-label on a tab begins with that tab's visible text rather than replacing it.
rules.runtime_check: Compute each tab's accessible name; assert it starts with the tab's visible text (WCAG 2.5.3 Label in Name).

rules.rule: Each tabpanel has `aria-labelledby` referencing the `id` of its tab.
rules.static_hint: Every role="tabpanel" carries aria-labelledby whose value is the id of its corresponding role="tab" element.

rules.rule: The selected tab has `aria-selected="true"` and every other tab has `aria-selected="false"`.
rules.static_hint: aria-selected is bound on every role="tab" element to an expression that resolves to "true" for exactly one tab and "false" for the rest.

rules.rule: The `"false"` value is set explicitly, including on a tab that holds focus without being selected under manual activation.
rules.static_hint: No branch renders a role="tab" element without an aria-selected attribute.

rules.rule: Each tab has `aria-controls` referencing the `id` of its tabpanel.
rules.static_hint: Every role="tab" carries aria-controls whose value is the id of its role="tabpanel".

rules.rule: The selected tab is distinguishable from unselected tabs by more than color (e.g., weight, an underline, or an icon), per `global.use-of-color`.
rules.runtime_check: Compare computed styles of the selected and an unselected tab; assert at least one non-color property differs (font-weight, border, text-decoration, or an added child element).

rules.rule: The tab set implements one activation model consistently (see Customizable for choosing one).
rules.llm_eval_question: When runtime cannot exercise the component, do the arrow-key path and the click path resolve to the same activation model?
rules.runtime_check: Arrow to an adjacent tab and record whether selection changed; click a third tab and record the same. Assert both paths agree on whether focus alone selects.

rules.rule: Under automatic activation, arrow-key movement also selects the newly focused tab and displays its panel.
rules.runtime_check: Under automatic activation, press Right Arrow; assert the newly focused tab has aria-selected="true" and its panel is the visible one.

rules.rule: Under manual activation, arrow-key movement changes focus only, and the selected tab and displayed panel do not change until Enter or Space.
rules.runtime_check: Under manual activation, arrow to an unselected tab and assert aria-selected and the visible panel are unchanged; press Enter and assert both update.

rules.rule: Right Arrow and Left Arrow move focus between tabs and wrap at the ends.
rules.llm_eval_question: When runtime cannot exercise the component, do the ArrowRight and ArrowLeft branches move focus one tab in each direction and wrap at both ends?
rules.runtime_check: Focus the first tab; press Left Arrow and assert focus is on the last tab; press Right Arrow and assert focus returns to the first.

rules.rule: In a vertical tablist, Down Arrow performs as Right Arrow and Up Arrow performs as Left Arrow.
rules.runtime_check: In a vertical tablist, press Down Arrow and Up Arrow; assert focus moves to the next and previous tab respectively.

rules.rule: A horizontal tablist leaves Up and Down Arrow alone so the page can still scroll.
rules.runtime_check: In a horizontal tablist, focus a tab and press Down Arrow; assert focus does not move and the page scroll position changes.

rules.rule: Home moves focus to the first tab and End moves focus to the last tab.
rules.runtime_check: From a middle tab, press Home and assert focus is on the first tab; press End and assert focus is on the last tab.

rules.rule: Enter or Space activates the focused tab when it was not already activated on focus.
rules.runtime_check: Under manual activation, arrow to an unselected tab and press Enter; assert its panel becomes visible. Repeat with Space.

rules.rule: Tab moves focus out of the tablist to the next element in the page tab sequence, never to another tab.
rules.static_hint: Exactly one tab is bound to tabindex="0"; all others are bound to tabindex="-1".
rules.runtime_check: Focus a tab and press Tab; assert focus leaves the tablist and does not land on another role="tab" element.

rules.rule: The selected tab has `tabindex="0"` and every other tab has `tabindex="-1"`, so the tablist is a single Tab stop.
rules.static_hint: tabindex on each tab is bound to the selection state, resolving to 0 for the selected tab and -1 for the rest.

rules.rule: When the tabpanel's content begins with a non-focusable element, the tabpanel has `tabindex="0"`, so that Tab from the tablist reaches the panel content instead of skipping past it.
rules.static_hint: Tabpanels whose first content element is not natively focusable carry tabindex="0".
rules.runtime_check: With a panel whose content starts non-focusable, focus the selected tab and press Tab; assert focus lands on the tabpanel element.

rules.rule: The focus indicator on a focused tab is distinguishable from the selected-tab styling.
rules.runtime_check: Under manual activation, arrow to an unselected tab; assert its computed focus styling differs from the selected tab's styling.

rules.rule: Do not leave a tabpanel visible while its tab has `aria-selected="false"` (and vice versa).
rules.runtime_check: After each tab activation, assert the visible tabpanel is the one referenced by the tab whose aria-selected is "true", and no other panel is visible.

rules.rule: Do not derive arrow-key movement from the selected tab's index instead of the focused tab's index.
rules.llm_eval_question: Does the arrow-key handler compute the next index from the index of the tab that currently has focus, rather than from the selected-tab state variable?
rules.runtime_check: Under manual activation, arrow twice in one direction from the selected tab; assert focus advanced two tabs rather than returning to the first neighbor.

rules.rule: Do not move focus off the activated tab.
rules.runtime_check: Activate each tab by click and by Enter; assert document.activeElement remains that role="tab" element and the document URL is unchanged.

rules.rule: The live region container must be present in the DOM when the page/view loads.
rules.static_hint: Live region element is rendered unconditionally at mount, not created when a toast fires.
rules.runtime_check: Load the page with no toast triggered; assert the live region container already exists (empty) in the DOM.

rules.rule: The toast message must be announced via `role="status"`, or an equivalent such as `aria-live="polite"` and `aria-atomic="true"`.
rules.static_hint: Live region carries role="status", or aria-live="polite" plus aria-atomic="true".

rules.rule: When a toast is triggered, its message text must be injected into the existing live region container.
rules.runtime_check: Trigger a toast; assert the message text appears inside the pre-existing live region element (same node, not a new container).

rules.rule: The toast must not move focus automatically when it appears.
rules.runtime_check: Focus an element, trigger a toast; assert document.activeElement is unchanged.

rules.rule: The toast must disappear automatically (recommended ~5 seconds).
rules.runtime_check: Trigger a toast and wait past the timeout; assert the toast is no longer visible without user action.

rules.rule: The live region text must be cleared when the toast dismisses to avoid stale messages being discovered later.
rules.runtime_check: After the toast dismisses, assert the live region container's text content is empty.

rules.rule: If a dismiss button is present, it must not steal focus when the toast appears.
rules.runtime_check: Focus an element, trigger a toast with a dismiss button; assert focus does not move to the dismiss button.

rules.rule: Do not mount/unmount the live region container based on toast visibility.
rules.static_hint: Flag conditional rendering of the live region element tied to toast state.
rules.runtime_check: Trigger and dismiss toasts; assert the live region element is the same persistent DOM node throughout.

rules.rule: Do not move focus into the toast when it appears.
rules.runtime_check: Trigger a toast; assert document.activeElement never becomes the toast or a descendant of it.

rules.rule: Do not use `role="alertdialog"`.
rules.static_hint: Flag role="alertdialog" on the toast or its container.

rules.rule: The toast must not contain buttons or elements that require user action (use `snackbar` or `dialog` instead).
rules.static_hint: Flag interactive elements inside the toast (an optional dismiss button per the Must Haves is the only tolerated control).
rules.llm_eval_question: Does the toast's content demand a user decision or action (confirm, undo, input), meaning it should be a snackbar or dialog instead?

rules.rule: The tooltip bubble is an element with `role="tooltip"` and a stable `id`.
rules.static_hint: Tooltip element carries role="tooltip" and a deterministic id.

rules.rule: The trigger references the tooltip with `aria-describedby` pointing to the tooltip's `id`.
rules.static_hint: Trigger's aria-describedby IDREF equals the tooltip's id.

rules.rule: The tooltip supplements the accessible name, it does not replace it. The trigger has its own accessible name (e.g., visible text or `aria-label`).
rules.static_hint: Trigger has a non-empty accessible name independent of the tooltip; tooltip is referenced by aria-describedby, not aria-labelledby.
rules.llm_eval_question: Is the tooltip content supplemental description rather than serving as the trigger's only name?

rules.rule: The tooltip appears on both pointer hover and keyboard focus of the trigger.
rules.runtime_check: Hover the trigger; assert the tooltip shows. Separately, keyboard-focus the trigger; assert the tooltip shows.

rules.rule: Esc dismisses the tooltip whether it was opened by pointer hover or by keyboard focus, and does not move pointer hover or keyboard focus (dismissible).
rules.runtime_check: Show the tooltip via hover, press Esc; assert it hides. Repeat via focus; assert it hides and document.activeElement is unchanged.

rules.rule: Bind the Esc handler at the document level, not only on the trigger, so it works when the tooltip is shown by hover and the trigger does not hold focus.
rules.static_hint: Esc keydown listener is attached to document while the tooltip is visible, not solely to the trigger element.
rules.runtime_check: With focus elsewhere on the page, hover the trigger and press Esc; assert the tooltip dismisses.

rules.rule: When the trigger has keyboard focus, the trigger keeps focus after dismissal.
rules.runtime_check: Focus the trigger, press Esc to dismiss; assert document.activeElement is still the trigger.

rules.rule: The tooltip remains visible while the pointer is over the trigger or over the tooltip, and while the trigger has focus (hoverable and persistent).
rules.runtime_check: Move the pointer from the trigger onto the tooltip bubble; assert it stays visible. Hold keyboard focus on the trigger; assert it stays visible.

rules.rule: Track hover and focus as independent conditions and keep the tooltip open while either is active, so a stray pointer movement does not hide it while the trigger still has keyboard focus.
rules.static_hint: Visibility state derives from hover OR focus flags, not a single shared boolean.
rules.runtime_check: Focus the trigger, then move the pointer across and off the trigger; assert the tooltip remains visible while focus is held.

rules.rule: The tooltip is not focusable and contains plain text only, with no interactive content.
rules.static_hint: Tooltip has no tabindex and no interactive descendants; content is text-only.
rules.runtime_check: Tab through the page with the tooltip visible; assert the tooltip never receives focus.

rules.rule: Do not place interactive content (links, buttons, form controls) in a tooltip.
rules.static_hint: Flag any interactive element inside the role="tooltip" element.

rules.rule: Do not rely on the native `title` attribute as the tooltip; it is not keyboard-accessible and is announced inconsistently.
rules.static_hint: Flag title attributes used as the tooltip mechanism on the trigger.

rules.rule: Do not make the tooltip vanish when the pointer moves from the trigger toward the tooltip; it must be hoverable.
rules.runtime_check: Traverse the pointer from trigger to tooltip across the gap; assert the tooltip does not hide during the traversal or while hovered.

rules.rule: Do not show the tooltip on hover only; it must also appear on keyboard focus.
rules.runtime_check: Without any pointer input, keyboard-focus the trigger; assert the tooltip appears.

rules.rule: Do not hide the tooltip on `onMouseLeave` while the trigger still has keyboard focus; hover and focus must be tracked independently.
rules.static_hint: Flag mouseleave handlers that hide unconditionally without checking the focus flag.
rules.runtime_check: Focus the trigger, hover it, then move the pointer away; assert the tooltip stays visible while focus remains.

rules.rule: Do not use `role="menu"` on the tooltip.
rules.static_hint: Flag role="menu" on the tooltip element.

rules.rule: Do not leave the tooltip visible after the trigger has lost focus and the pointer has left both the trigger and the tooltip.
rules.runtime_check: Blur the trigger and move the pointer off both trigger and tooltip; assert the tooltip hides.

rules.rule: When a component receives keyboard focus, the focused element is not entirely hidden by author-created content such as sticky headers, sticky footers, or the component's own overlapping chrome (WCAG 2.4.11 Focus Not Obscured, Minimum).
rules.runtime_check: Tab through the page with sticky regions rendered; after each focus change assert the focused element's rect is at least partially unobscured via elementFromPoint.

rules.rule: Components with their own sticky or floating sub-regions (e.g., a frozen header row or column) keep the focused element scrolled or offset into a visible area.
rules.runtime_check: Within a component having a frozen header row or column, move focus behind it; assert the component scrolls or offsets so the focused element is visible.

rules.rule: Each keyboard-focusable user interface component must have a visible focus indicator when it receives keyboard focus.
rules.runtime_check: Keyboard-focus every focusable element; assert its computed style changes visibly on focus (outline, box-shadow, border, or background).

rules.rule: The focus indicator must have a contrast ratio of at least 3:1 against adjacent colors.
rules.runtime_check: For each focus indicator, compute its contrast against the adjacent colors; assert at least 3:1.

rules.rule: Do not make the focus indicator so subtle that users cannot quickly identify which element currently has focus.
rules.llm_eval_question: Would the focus indicator be quickly noticeable to a sighted keyboard user, rather than a change that meets 3:1 but reads as incidental?

rules.rule: Do not rely on hover-only styles as the only visible indicator of focus.
rules.static_hint: Flag a component with a :hover style whose focus state has no :focus-visible or :focus rule.

rules.rule: Do not ship focus styles without a `forced-colors` override — Windows High Contrast Mode users will lose the custom colors and be left with browser defaults that may not match the design's contrast intent.
rules.static_hint: Any authored :focus-visible style is paired with a @media (forced-colors: active) override using the Highlight system color.

rules.rule: Each page (route/view/document) has one level 1 heading, or `<h1>`, that identifies the main topic of the page.
rules.static_hint: Exactly one h1 (or role=heading aria-level=1) exists per route.
rules.llm_eval_question: Does the h1 identify the main topic of this page?

rules.rule: Headings are nested in a logical order according to the relationships of the content they introduce.
rules.static_hint: Heading levels increase by at most one when moving deeper; flag a skip such as h2 followed by h4.

rules.rule: If text visually functions as a heading, it must be marked up as a heading element rather than only styled to look like one.
rules.llm_eval_question: Is there text styled as a section title (large or bold, introducing content) that is not marked up as a heading element?

rules.rule: If footer links are grouped under visible group titles (e.g., "Company", "Support", "Legal"), each group title is a level 2 heading (`<h2>`).
rules.static_hint: Footer link-group titles are h2 elements, not styled divs or spans.

rules.rule: Headings are descriptive of the content they introduce.
rules.llm_eval_question: Does each heading describe the content that follows it, rather than being generic ("Section", "More")?

rules.rule: Do not use heading elements only to make text look larger or bolder.
rules.llm_eval_question: Is any heading element used for visual emphasis on text that does not introduce a section?

rules.rule: When site or app navigation is present on a page (route/view/document), this is contained inside a `<nav>` (or `role="navigation"`) landmark, which is contained inside a `<header>` (or `role="banner"`) landmark.
rules.static_hint: Navigation link groups sit inside a <nav> or role="navigation", which is inside a <header> or role="banner".

rules.rule: If a single set of navigation is present, then it should be labeled (e.g., `<nav aria-label="primary">`).
rules.static_hint: The nav landmark carries aria-label or aria-labelledby.

rules.rule: If more than one set of navigation is present - e.g., primary and secondary or breadcrumbs - then each `navigation` landmark must be labeled (e.g., `<nav aria-label="primary">`, `<nav aria-label="secondary">`, `<nav aria-label="breadcrumbs">`).
rules.static_hint: When more than one nav landmark exists, every one carries a label, and no two labels are identical.
rules.llm_eval_question: Does each nav landmark's label distinguish it from the others by purpose?

rules.rule: When a footer is present - i.e., a section at the bottom of the page with information relevant to the entire site, such as a sitemap or navigation links - this is contained inside a `<footer>` (or `role="contentinfo"`) landmark.
rules.static_hint: Site-wide footer content sits inside a <footer> or role="contentinfo" that is not nested inside <main>.

rules.rule: A `<main>` (or `role="main"`) landmark must always be present.
rules.static_hint: Exactly one <main> or role="main" element exists in the rendered page.

rules.rule: The `main` landmark contains the dominant content of the page, which directly relates to or expands upon the central topic of the page, or the central functionality of an application.
rules.llm_eval_question: Does the main landmark wrap the page's dominant content, rather than a fragment of it or the whole page including header and footer?

rules.rule: If site or app navigation is present at the top of the page or view (i.e., `header`), and/or a footer (`footer`) is present at the bottom of the page, the `main` landmark should wrap all content between `header` and `footer` content.
rules.static_hint: No content sits between the header and footer outside the main landmark.

rules.rule: The `main` landmark must be a sibling of the `header` and/or `footer` containers.
rules.static_hint: main, header, and footer share a parent; none is nested inside another.

rules.rule: If the page contains complementary content - i.e., content that is only indirectly related to the page's main content - this is contained inside an `<aside>` (or `role="complementary"`) landmark.
rules.static_hint: Sidebar-style regions are marked up as <aside> or role="complementary".
rules.llm_eval_question: Is this region only indirectly related to the main content, making it complementary rather than part of main?

rules.rule: If present, the `aside` landmark should be a sibling to the `main` landmark, and to the `header` and/or `footer`, if present.
rules.static_hint: aside shares a parent with main, header, and footer; it is not nested inside main.

rules.rule: Do not use multiple `main` landmarks on the same page.
rules.static_hint: Flag a page with more than one <main> or role="main".

rules.rule: Visual information needed to identify a user interface component - such as control boundaries - must have a contrast ratio of at least 3:1 against adjacent colors.
rules.runtime_check: Compute the contrast of each control's boundary or background against the adjacent surface; assert at least 3:1.

rules.rule: Meaningful graphical objects must have a contrast ratio of at least 3:1 against adjacent colors when their appearance is needed to understand the content.
rules.llm_eval_question: Is this graphic meaningful — needed to understand the content or identify a state — rather than decorative?
rules.runtime_check: For each graphic judged meaningful, compute its contrast against adjacent colors; assert at least 3:1.

rules.rule: Each page (route/view/document) sets a descriptive page title that reflects the central topic of the current page.
rules.llm_eval_question: Does the title name the central topic of this specific page, rather than being a site-wide or placeholder string?
rules.runtime_check: Visit each route; assert document.title is non-empty and differs from the other routes' titles.

rules.rule: The page title begins with the name of the current page and is followed by the name of the site.
rules.llm_eval_question: Is the first segment the page name and the last the site name, rather than the reverse?
rules.runtime_check: Read document.title; assert it contains a separator with content on both sides.

rules.rule: Page name and site name should be separated using a clear visual character, such as a hyphen, emdash, or vertical pipe.
rules.runtime_check: Assert document.title matches a page/site split on a hyphen, em dash, or vertical pipe.

rules.rule: Page name should be similar to the `<h1>` text on the page.
rules.llm_eval_question: Do the title's page-name segment and the h1 refer to the same thing, allowing for reasonable shortening?
rules.runtime_check: Compare the title's page-name segment with the page's h1 text content.

rules.rule: Do not leave the page title as a generic placeholder across routes.
rules.runtime_check: Visit several routes and collect document.title; assert the titles are not identical and none is a framework default (e.g., "React App", "Document").

rules.rule: Where a component's rules dictate the use of "offscreen text", then the snippet below must be included as a CSS class: `.sr-only`.
rules.static_hint: A .sr-only class is defined with the clip/position/1px-size/overflow-hidden property set; flag a definition that omits any of them.

rules.rule: Do not hide offscreen text using `display: none` or `visibility: hidden` when it is needed for an accessible name.
rules.static_hint: Flag display:none or visibility:hidden on any element referenced by aria-labelledby/aria-describedby or serving as offscreen label text.
rules.runtime_check: Compute the accessible name of controls named by offscreen text; assert the text contributes rather than resolving to empty.

rules.rule: Text and images of text must have sufficient contrast against their background.
rules.runtime_check: Compute the contrast ratio of every text node against its effective background; assert at least 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large-scale text (18pt regular or 14pt bold).

rules.rule: Do not use color as the only visual means of conveying information, indicating an action, prompting a response, or distinguishing a visual element (WCAG 1.4.1).
rules.llm_eval_question: Is any information, action, or distinction conveyed by color with no accompanying text, shape, icon, or other non-color cue?

rules.rule: When a component renders a meaningful state visually (e.g., selected, active, current, invalid, pressed), that state is distinguishable by something in addition to color, such as an icon, checkmark, shape, underline, or text.
rules.llm_eval_question: For each visually rendered state, is there a non-color cue (icon, shape, underline, text) in addition to the color change?
